slot.brief: Blocks in contact or connected by string on frictionless surface; find acceleration then contact/tension force

stem: A $3\ \text{kg}$ block and a $6\ \text{kg}$ block are joined by a light string on a frictionless horizontal table. A horizontal force of $27\ \text{N}$ pulls the $3\ \text{kg}$ block away from the other block. What are the acceleration of the blocks and the string tension?

verdicts.working: Total mass = 3 + 6 = 9 kg, so acceleration = 27/9 = 3 m s^-2. For the 6 kg block, tension = 6 × 3 = 18 N.

working:
$a=\dfrac{27}{3+6}=3\ \text{m s}^{-2}$
$T=6a=18\ \text{N}$

Independent check: Total mass = 3 + 6 = 9 kg, so acceleration = 27/9 = 3 m s^-2. For the 6 kg block, tension = 6 × 3 = 18 N.
solution:
For the two-block system, $a=\dfrac{F}{m_1+m_2}=\dfrac{27}{3+6}=3\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
For the $6\ \text{kg}$ block, $T=m_2a=6(3)=18\ \text{N}$.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses an incorrect system acceleration and corresponding tension.
